description:
Project Overview

TU Delft is looking for two PhD candidates to join the Curious Beams Lab and develop a new approach to imaging material surfaces with electrons. The positions are part of BEAMSurf: Diffractive Atomic-Scale Surface Imaging with Backscattered Electrons, an ERC Starting Grant project led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides.

Surfaces control many properties and processes that determine material functionality, from chemical reactions in catalysis to interfaces in nanoelectronic devices. BEAMSurf will develop a new scanning electron microscope that uses coherent backscattered electrons for diffractive imaging of surfaces, with the potential to overcome conventional resolution limits for low-energy SEM.

The Two PhD Roles

  • PhD 1 - Electron Optics and Experimental Imaging: design, characterise and integrate miniature electron-optical components into a high-vacuum SEM, separating the backscattered-electron signal from the primary beam.
  • PhD 2 - Computational Imaging and Surface Science: develop forward models and inverse-scattering approaches for reflection-mode electron imaging, moving beyond static images towards surfaces as they evolve.

Research Environment

The Curious Beams Lab is part of the Microscopy and Instrumentation Techniques (MInT) cluster of the Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft, Faculty of Applied Sciences. The cluster works across electron microscopy, from semiconductor inspection to cryogenic electron microscopy, with access to state-of-the-art field-emission SEMs and FIB-SEMs, including a new microscope acquired for this project.

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral employee (full-time, 38 hours/week)
SalaryEUR 3,204 to EUR 4,051 gross per month, increasing from the first to the fourth year, based on the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO).
Additional pay8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus.
DurationFour years in principle, split into two contracts: an initial 18-month contract with a go/no-go assessment, followed by 30 months after a satisfactory assessment.
Project fundingERC Starting Grant (BEAMSurf); the team also includes a postdoctoral researcher leading instrumentation development.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMSc or equivalent in physics, applied physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, computer science, or a closely related field.
InterestStrong interest in experimental physics, electron microscopy, imaging science or a related area.
Electron-optics trackExperience or interest in electron optics, electromagnetic simulation, nanofabrication, MEMS, vacuum systems or experimental microscopy is particularly valuable.
Computational trackExperience or interest in scientific programming, numerical simulation, inverse problems, computational imaging, diffraction or materials characterisation is particularly valuable.
AvailabilityCandidates should be available to start in 2027, with some flexibility around the exact start date.

How to Apply

Apply online through the official vacancy page using the application button. Applications sent by email or post are not processed. Prepare a CV and a motivation letter; check the advert for any additional documents such as transcripts or references.

About TU Delft

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. The Faculty of Applied Sciences provides an interdisciplinary environment spanning multiple imaging modalities, wavelengths and length scales, including extreme ultraviolet imaging, optical super-resolution, ultrasound and MRI, as well as AI-based medical imaging.

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.
